rules.statement: A continuing invasion of a subsisting right constitutes in truth a continuing cause of action, and the remedy for such an invasion is not barred by limitation if instituted within three years from when the fresh cause of action arises.
rules.supporting_quote: "Indeed, the contrary view would indirectly produce the anomalous result of converting the provisions of section 10 into a weapon for the extinction of a right which cannot in law be extinguished by prescription. Be that as it may, the circumstances of the present case, interpreted by reference to the conduct of the parties, are clearly distinguishable from those which arose in the earlier decisions."

meta.parties: Kirikitta Saranankara Thero v. Medegama Dhammananda Thero
